newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn says EU leaders firmed up stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Quinn says EU leaders firmed up stability pact.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Friday that European Union leaders had firmed up a proposed budget pact for economies after the single currency is introduced.
This includes setting a high 2 percent of economic shrinkage as a sign that countries were facing extraordinary difficulties and should be exempt from fines for overspending.

"We are now able to say to the citizens of Europe and to the markets that we have agreed the legal basis, the ERM mark 2 and the terms and conditions of the stability and growth pact," Quinn told a news conference.
He was referring to a package of measures needed by the EU to provide the framework for economic and monetary union.

The decision came after an 11-hour emergency finance ministers meeting and close to a day of negotiations by EU leaders forced by German insistence that there should be water-tight rules for stopping excessive deficits.

The agreement was that a fall in economic growth of two percent or more of Gross Domestic Product would be considered to be exceptional enough for a country to avoid fines. If the fall in GDP was between 0.75 percent and two percent, ministers could rule on whether fines should be levied.
